newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis shelter from Hizbollah salvo, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Israelis shelter from Hizbollah salvo, no injuries.

text.p: Many residents of northern Israel spent a night in secure rooms and bomb shelters after guerrillas in Lebanon fired salvoes of rockets at army positions on the border, Israeli security sources said on Thursday.
No one was injured in the wave of mortar and rocket attacks and Israel's northern army commander Major General Amiram Levine said it was unclear if any rockets landed in Israel.

Levine said Hizbollah units fired about 40 rounds of mortars and Katyusha rockets at three Israeli army strongpoints along Israel's nothern border with Lebanon shortly before midnight (2100 GMT) on Wednesday.
"They didn't shoot into the area of Israel. Maybe one or a few of the rounds fell in the area. So I believe that we will succeed to keep the area quiet," Levine told reporters.
An army statement said there were no casualties and no reports of damage.
The rockets were fired one day after Hizbollah (Party of God) threatened to carry out suicide bombings inside Israel and Arab land occupied by the Jewish state.

Hizbollah is fighting to drive some 1,000 Israel troops and their local Lebanese militia allies from Israel's 15-km (nine-mile) occupation zone in south Lebanon. The occupation zone is a site of frequent rocket attacks, clashes and bombs.
Israel and Hizbollah undertook not to fire on civilian targets as part of a 1996 ceasefire that ended a 17-day Israeli onslaught in which about 200 people -- mainly Lebanese civilians -- were killed.
"It's a war in the area. We're trying to keep the understanding...and we hope everything will be as usual as soon as possible," Levine said.

In South Lebanon, pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army sources said a Hizbollah car bomb killed a pro-Israeli militiaman on Thursday. Security sources said one Lebanese civilian was killed and two wounded by retaliatory Israeli shelling.
Israeli warplanes on Tuesday blasted suspected Hizbollah targets in Lebanon's eastern Bekaa Valley, killing two Lebanese civilians and wounding four, security sources said.
On Monday, Israeli commandos in helicopters backed by planes raided suspected Hizbollah targets in southern Lebanon, triggering fierce clashes at Kfour in Nabatiyeh outside the zone.
Five Hizbollah guerrillas were killed later by three roadside bombs planted by Israeli commandos. Five civilians were wounded in the bombings.
